transferReply: Start a nest egg early, even if it's small.
nuance: Countable and always singular in practice. It suggests long, steady saving rather than a windfall.

meaning: Noticeably better than others of the same kind.
easyEnglish: Noticeably better than others of the same kind.
japanese: 同じ種類のなかで、ひと味上である。
cue: One supplier's samples are clearly better. Report it.
reply: Their finishing is a cut above the other two.
transferCue: Recommend a local restaurant.
transferReply: It's a cut above the other places on that street.
nuance: Comparative, so it usually needs a point of comparison. Quieter praise than the best.

meaning: More than what was required.
easyEnglish: More than what was required.
japanese: 求められた以上のことをする。
cue: A colleague stayed to help a customer after closing. Recognise it.
reply: That was above and beyond what we ask of anyone.
transferCue: Thank a neighbour who did more than expected.
transferReply: Fixing the gate as well was above and beyond.
nuance: Often with go: go above and beyond. Warm recognition, common in workplace praise.

meaning: Considering everything together.
easyEnglish: Considering everything together.
japanese: 全体として見れば。
cue: An event had problems but succeeded. Sum it up.
reply: All in all, it went better than we expected.
transferCue: Summarise a mixed holiday.
transferReply: All in all, I'd go back but in a different season.
nuance: Usually opens a summary sentence, followed by a comma. It signals a balanced overall judgement.

meaning: Very popular at the moment.
easyEnglish: Very popular at the moment.
japanese: 今、大流行している。
cue: A friend asks why a particular bag is everywhere.
reply: That shape is all the rage this year.
transferCue: Describe a food trend in your area.
transferReply: Sourdough was all the rage here two winters ago.
nuance: Informal and often implies the popularity will not last. Used after be.

meaning: Something you only start to like after trying it several times.
easyEnglish: Something you only start to like after trying it several times.
japanese: 慣れてくると好きになる、癖のあるもの。
cue: A guest is unsure about a strong local cheese. Reassure them.
reply: It's an acquired taste. Try it with the honey.
transferCue: Describe a film style you grew to like.
transferReply: Long takes were an acquired taste for me.
nuance: Polite about something not immediately likeable, for food, art or even people.

meaning: Measured in a straight line, not by road.
easyEnglish: Measured in a straight line, not by road.
japanese: 道のりではなく、直線距離で。
cue: A friend asks how far two towns are apart.
reply: Eight kilometres as the crow flies, but twenty by road.
transferCue: Explain why a nearby place takes so long to reach.
transferReply: It's close as the crow flies, but there's a river between us.
frame: X kilometres as the crow flies
nuance: Follows a distance. Fixed wording, and it usually sets up a contrast with the real journey.

meaning: Unable to understand or know what to do.
easyEnglish: Unable to understand or know what to do.
japanese: どうすればよいか分からず、困っている。
cue: A recurring fault has no obvious cause. Admit it honestly.
reply: I'm at a loss to explain why it only happens on Mondays.
transferCue: Describe your reaction to unexpectedly kind news.
transferReply: I was at a loss for words when they offered to help.
frame: Be at a loss to do something / for words
nuance: Followed by to plus a verb, or by for words. It admits difficulty without blaming anyone.

meaning: Whatever effort or sacrifice is needed.
easyEnglish: Whatever effort or sacrifice is needed.
japanese: どんな犠牲を払ってでも。
cue: One requirement cannot be compromised. State it clearly.
reply: We need to protect the delivery date at all costs.
transferCue: Describe a boundary you keep in your week.
transferReply: I protect Sunday mornings at all costs.
nuance: Costs is always plural. Strong, so reserve it for genuine priorities or it loses force.

meaning: At risk of being lost if things go wrong.
easyEnglish: At risk of being lost if things go wrong.
japanese: うまくいかなければ失われる、危うい状態にある。
cue: A decision affects the team's whole year. Explain the weight of it.
reply: There's a lot at stake, so let's take an extra day.
transferCue: Describe why a conversation felt difficult.
transferReply: Our friendship was at stake, which made it hard to be honest.
nuance: The thing at risk is the subject. It raises the stakes of a discussion, so use it where the risk is real.

meaning: One immediately after another.
easyEnglish: One immediately after another.
japanese: 間を置かずに、続けて。
cue: Someone asks whether you have a free slot this afternoon.
reply: I'm back to back until four, sorry.
transferCue: Describe a busy weekend of events.
transferReply: We had two weddings back to back in June.
nuance: Written back-to-back with hyphens before a noun. It describes scheduling, not physical position, in this sense.

meaning: Produce good results after a long time.
easyEnglish: Produce good results after a long time.
japanese: 時間をかけた努力が、実を結ぶ。
cue: A long outreach effort finally brought partners. Report it.
reply: Two years of visits have started to bear fruit.
transferCue: Describe a slow personal project.
transferReply: The garden is finally bearing fruit in its third year.
nuance: Fruit stays singular and takes no article. It implies patience, so it suits slow results.

meaning: Politely disagree.
easyEnglish: Politely disagree.
japanese: 失礼ながら、意見が違うと述べる。
cue: A colleague says the old process was faster. Disagree politely.
reply: I beg to differ. The logs show it took two days longer.
transferCue: Disagree with a friend about a film.
transferReply: I beg to differ — the ending made the whole thing work.
nuance: Slightly formal and often lightly ironic. Usually a whole sentence, followed by your reason.

meaning: Doing something late is better than not doing it.
easyEnglish: Doing something late is better than not doing it.
japanese: 遅くなっても、やらないよりはましだ。
cue: A friend apologises for a birthday message a week late.
reply: Better late than never. Thank you.
transferCue: Comment on starting a new skill in your forties.
transferReply: I started at forty-two, but better late than never.
nuance: A set phrase, usually forgiving. Said about someone else's lateness it can sound pointed.

meaning: It is wiser to be careful than to risk regret.
easyEnglish: It is wiser to be careful than to risk regret.
japanese: あとで後悔するより、用心したほうがいい。
cue: A friend thinks a second copy of the documents is excessive.
reply: Better safe than sorry. Print one for your bag.
transferCue: Explain why you left early for an appointment.
transferReply: I left an hour early — better safe than sorry.
nuance: A set phrase justifying caution. It works best with the specific precaution you are suggesting.

meaning: Wait patiently for the right moment.
easyEnglish: Wait patiently for the right moment.
japanese: 好機を待って、じっと構える。
cue: A colleague wants to raise a proposal during a tense week. Advise waiting.
reply: Bide your time until the review is over.
transferCue: Describe how you handled a slow market.
transferReply: We bided our time and bought in the autumn.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Bide is used almost only in this phrase.

meaning: Be the first to do something that others then follow.
easyEnglish: Be the first to do something that others then follow.
japanese: 先駆けとなって、道を切り開く。
cue: A team's method has been copied across the company. Recognise it.
reply: Your team blazed a trail with the shared checklist.
transferCue: Describe an early figure in a field.
transferReply: She blazed a trail for women in structural engineering.
nuance: For introduces who follows. Admiring, and often used about people who went first in difficult conditions.

meaning: Suddenly become very angry.
easyEnglish: Suddenly become very angry.
japanese: かんしゃくを起こす。
cue: You reacted badly to a repeated mistake. Reflect on it.
reply: I blew my top over the third missed deadline, which didn't help.
transferCue: Warn a colleague how a client may react.
transferReply: He might blow his top when he sees the invoice.
nuance: Informal, and the possessive follows the subject. It describes a sudden outburst rather than lasting anger.

meaning: Tell someone about something important, often bad.
easyEnglish: Tell someone about something important, often bad.
japanese: 重要な知らせを、本人に伝える。
cue: A decision affects a colleague who has not heard yet. Offer to tell them.
reply: I'll break the news to her before the meeting.
transferCue: Describe telling a family member about a move.
transferReply: We broke the news over dinner so everyone heard it together.
nuance: To introduces the person told. It implies care about how the news lands, not just informing.

meaning: Do something that makes people notice and remember you.
easyEnglish: Do something that makes people notice and remember you.
japanese: 存在を認められる成果を残す。
cue: A new colleague asks how to build a reputation in the team.
reply: You'll make your mark faster by finishing one thing well than by starting five.
transferCue: Describe an artist's first exhibition.
transferReply: She made her mark with a single room of small drawings.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and on introduces the field. It is about recognition, not about winning.

meaning: Encounter someone as strong or skilled as you.
easyEnglish: Encounter someone as strong or skilled as you.
japanese: 自分に匹敵する相手に出会う。
cue: A famously fast colleague was outpaced by a newcomer. Comment.
reply: He's finally met his match on the crossword.
transferCue: Describe a close game between two strong teams.
transferReply: They met their match in the semi-final.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually admiring and light, not a warning.

meaning: Notice every detail and every opportunity.
easyEnglish: Notice every detail and every opportunity.
japanese: 細かい点も好機も、決して見逃さない。
cue: A colleague spotted an error nobody else saw. Praise them.
reply: You don't miss a trick. That was on page eleven.
transferCue: Describe a shopkeeper who remembers every customer.
transferReply: He doesn't miss a trick — he knew I'd been away.
nuance: Almost always negative in form but complimentary in meaning. Trick stays singular.

meaning: People with money get what they want.
easyEnglish: People with money get what they want.
japanese: 金がものを言う。
cue: A late application was accepted after a large donation. Comment drily.
reply: Money talks, apparently.
transferCue: Explain how one bidder won a contested sale.
transferReply: Three of us wanted the flat, but money talks.
nuance: A set saying, usually critical. Money is the subject and takes no article.

meaning: Usually; most of the time.
easyEnglish: Usually; most of the time.
japanese: たいていの場合は。
cue: A friend asks whether the bus is reliable.
reply: More often than not it's on time, but leave a margin.
transferCue: Describe a pattern you have noticed at work.
transferReply: More often than not, the problem is the input file.
nuance: Usually opens a sentence with a comma. It claims a tendency, not a rule, so it is a careful way to generalise.

meaning: Exactly level in a competition.
easyEnglish: Exactly level in a competition.
japanese: 競り合って、互角である。
cue: Two candidates scored almost identically. Describe the position.
reply: They're neck and neck after the second round.
transferCue: Describe two products competing in a market.
transferReply: The two brands have been neck and neck all year.
frame: Be neck and neck with someone
nuance: From horse racing. With introduces the rival, and it describes an ongoing contest rather than a result.

meaning: Two people clearly dislike each other.
easyEnglish: Two people clearly dislike each other.
japanese: 互いに好意を持っていない。
cue: Two colleagues avoid each other's meetings. Describe it discreetly.
reply: There's no love lost between those two.
transferCue: Explain why you seated two guests apart.
transferReply: There's no love lost there, so I split the table.
frame: There's no love lost between X and Y
nuance: Almost always with there's and between. An understatement: it means real dislike.

meaning: Know nothing at all about something.
easyEnglish: Know nothing at all about something.
japanese: まったく見当がつかない。
cue: Someone asks about a system you have never used. Be honest.
reply: I don't have a clue how that one works, sorry.
transferCue: Describe your first day in a new role.
transferReply: On day one I didn't have a clue where anything was.
frame: Not have a clue about something
nuance: Informal. About someone else it sounds dismissive; about yourself it is ordinary honesty.

meaning: Because you chose to, without being asked.
easyEnglish: Because you chose to, without being asked.
japanese: 言われたからではなく、自分の意思で。
cue: A colleague rewrote the guide without being asked. Recognise it.
reply: She did it of her own accord, which made it more impressive.
transferCue: Describe why a child started helping at home.
transferReply: He started clearing the table of his own accord.
frame: Do something of your own accord
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Slightly formal, and it emphasises that nobody asked.

meaning: At the same level or quality as something else.
easyEnglish: At the same level or quality as something else.
japanese: 〜と同等の水準にある。
cue: A cheaper supplier matches the quality of the expensive one. Report it.
reply: Their finish is on a par with the brand we use now.
transferCue: Compare two cities you have lived in.
transferReply: The transport there is on a par with Tokyo for reliability.
frame: Be on a par with something
nuance: Fixed as on a par, never on par in careful writing. With introduces the comparison.

meaning: Representing someone, or in their interest.
easyEnglish: Representing someone, or in their interest.
japanese: 〜を代表して。〜のために。
cue: You are thanking a team at an event where the lead is absent.
reply: On behalf of the whole team, thank you for coming.
transferCue: Explain why you are calling about someone else's account.
transferReply: I'm calling on behalf of my mother, who can't manage the phone.
nuance: Slightly formal. On behalf of means as a representative; on someone's behalf usually means for their benefit.

meaning: After reconsidering.
easyEnglish: After reconsidering.
japanese: 考え直してみると。
cue: You were about to order the same thing again. Change your mind aloud.
reply: On second thoughts, I'll try the other one.
transferCue: Revise a decision in a meeting.
transferReply: On second thoughts, let's leave that item until next week.
nuance: British keeps thoughts plural; American says on second thought. It opens a sentence and signals a change of mind.

meaning: Judging only by how something first appears.
easyEnglish: Judging only by how something first appears.
japanese: 一見したところでは。
cue: A proposal looks cheap until you read the terms. Introduce your doubt.
reply: On the face of it it's cheaper, but the support is extra.
transferCue: Describe a simple-looking task that took all day.
transferReply: On the face of it it was a ten-minute job.
nuance: Usually opens a sentence and sets up a but. It signals that a closer look changes the picture.

meaning: In case something unlikely turns out to be true.
easyEnglish: In case something unlikely turns out to be true.
japanese: もしかしたら、という望みをかけて。
cue: You messaged someone you barely know about a job. Explain why.
reply: I wrote on the off chance that they were still hiring.
transferCue: Describe taking an umbrella on a clear day.
transferReply: I took it on the off chance, and I was glad I did.
nuance: Followed by that plus a clause, or used alone. It lowers expectations, which makes a request easy to refuse.

meaning: Unlike anyone or anything else.
easyEnglish: Unlike anyone or anything else.
japanese: ほかに類を見ない、唯一無二の。
cue: A retiring colleague is hard to describe. Sum them up.
reply: He's one of a kind. Nobody else could have run that team.
transferCue: Describe a handmade object you own.
transferReply: The bowl is one of a kind, which is why I never use it.
nuance: Kind stays singular. Warm praise for people, plain description for objects.

meaning: Unusual or different from normal.
easyEnglish: Unusual or different from normal.
japanese: いつもと違って、普通ではない。
cue: You are asked whether you noticed anything strange yesterday.
reply: Nothing out of the ordinary, as far as I remember.
transferCue: Recommend a restaurant that surprised you.
transferReply: The menu is nothing out of the ordinary, but the cooking is excellent.
nuance: Very common with nothing. Neutral, so it works for both praise and reassurance.

meaning: Completely finished.
easyEnglish: Completely finished.
japanese: すっかり終わって、片がついている。
cue: A friend dreads a dental appointment. Encourage them to go early.
reply: Book the morning slot and it's over and done with by ten.
transferCue: Describe your feeling after a long legal process.
transferReply: I just want it over and done with.
nuance: More emphatic than finished, with a sense of relief. Fixed word order.

meaning: Make it easier for something to happen later.
easyEnglish: Make it easier for something to happen later.
japanese: あとに続くものの道筋をつける。
cue: An early trial made a bigger rollout possible. Describe its role.
reply: The pilot paved the way for the national rollout.
transferCue: Describe a law's effect on later changes.
transferReply: That ruling paved the way for everything that followed.
nuance: For introduces what follows. Usually positive, and used in hindsight about causes.

meaning: Say you support something without really acting on it.
easyEnglish: Say you support something without really acting on it.
japanese: 口先だけで支持して、実際には行動しない。
cue: A policy is announced but nothing changes. Say it plainly in a review.
reply: We pay lip service to flexibility but every meeting is at nine.
transferCue: Describe a company's environmental claims.
transferReply: They pay lip service to recycling and nothing more.
nuance: To introduces the idea. Critical, so it accuses the speaker of insincerity rather than error.

meaning: Select only what you want from what is available.
easyEnglish: Select only what you want from what is available.
japanese: 好きなものだけを選り好みする。
cue: A colleague wants only the easy items from a shared list. Object gently.
reply: We can't all pick and choose, or the hard ones never get done.
transferCue: Describe the advantage of an experienced professional.
transferReply: After twenty years she can pick and choose her projects.
nuance: Can be critical of fussiness or admiring of a strong position. The two verbs always stay together.

meaning: Find small faults in an argument or plan.
easyEnglish: Find small faults in an argument or plan.
japanese: 細かいあらを探して、批判する。
cue: A colleague only ever finds faults. Describe the pattern to a friend.
reply: He picks holes in everything without suggesting anything.
transferCue: Invite genuine criticism of your own draft.
transferReply: Please pick holes in this before I send it out.
nuance: In introduces the argument. Usually negative about the critic, unless you invite it about your own work.

meaning: Cooperate with what someone wants.
easyEnglish: Cooperate with what someone wants.
japanese: 相手の意向に沿って協力する。
cue: Another department has agreed to your timeline. Report it.
reply: Finance is playing ball, so we can start on the first.
transferCue: Describe a negotiation that stalled.
transferReply: They wouldn't play ball on the delivery date.
nuance: Informal. With introduces the other side, and it often appears in the negative: wouldn't play ball.

meaning: Act cleverly so you get what you want.
easyEnglish: Act cleverly so you get what you want.
japanese: うまく立ち回って、望む結果を得る。
cue: A colleague has a good chance at a promotion. Advise them.
reply: If you play your cards right, you'll be leading that team by spring.
transferCue: Describe how someone secured a good deal.
transferReply: She played her cards right and got the flat below asking price.
frame: If you play your cards right, …
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually in an if clause, predicting a good outcome.

meaning: The stage after which you cannot go back.
easyEnglish: The stage after which you cannot go back.
japanese: もう引き返せなくなる地点。
cue: A deposit is about to become non-refundable. Flag the moment.
reply: Friday is the point of no return on the booking.
transferCue: Describe a stage in a renovation.
transferReply: Once the wall came down we were past the point of no return.
frame: Reach / pass the point of no return
nuance: Used with reach, pass or be past. It names a moment, so pair it with a date or event.

meaning: Make an occasion less enjoyable.
easyEnglish: Make an occasion less enjoyable.
japanese: その場の雰囲気に水を差す。
cue: Rain arrived during an outdoor party. Describe the effect.
reply: The rain put a damper on the afternoon.
transferCue: Describe how news affected a celebration.
transferReply: That email put a damper on the whole evening.
nuance: The cause is the subject. British English also says dampener. It describes mood, not cancellation.

meaning: Hide your disappointment or worry.
easyEnglish: Hide your disappointment or worry.
japanese: つらさを隠して、平気なふりをする。
cue: A friend smiled through bad news all evening. Describe it later.
reply: She put on a brave face, but I could tell.
transferCue: Admit how you handled a disappointing result.
transferReply: I put on a brave face at work and cried on the train.
nuance: Sympathetic rather than critical. Face stays singular even about several people.

meaning: End something's chances completely.
easyEnglish: End something's chances completely.
japanese: 可能性を完全に断つ。
cue: An injury ended a friend's race plans. Describe it.
reply: The ankle put paid to the marathon this year.
transferCue: Describe why a trip was cancelled.
transferReply: The strike put paid to our travel plans.
nuance: British and fairly formal. The cause is the subject, and the result is final.

meaning: Give something your full attention and effort.
easyEnglish: Give something your full attention and effort.
japanese: 本気で取り組む。
cue: A friend doubts they could learn an instrument. Encourage them.
reply: You could learn it if you put your mind to it.
transferCue: Describe how a colleague learned a language quickly.
transferReply: He put his mind to it and was conversational within a year.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually encouraging, in an if clause or about past effort.

meaning: Fast to react or act.
easyEnglish: Fast to react or act.
japanese: 反応が早く、すぐに動ける。
cue: A colleague applied within an hour of the posting. Comment.
reply: You were quick off the mark with that application.
transferCue: Explain why you missed a limited offer.
transferReply: I wasn't quick off the mark and it sold out.
nuance: From racing. The opposite is slow off the mark, and both describe reaction speed rather than overall pace.

meaning: Think very hard to remember or work something out.
easyEnglish: Think very hard to remember or work something out.
japanese: 思い出そうと、必死に頭をしぼる。
cue: You cannot remember where you left a key. Describe the effort.
reply: I've been racking my brains all morning about that key.
transferCue: Ask a colleague to help recall a detail.
transferReply: Rack your brains — who chaired the meeting in March?
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and brains stays plural. Spelled rack, not wrack.

meaning: Warn people about a danger or problem.
easyEnglish: Warn people about a danger or problem.
japanese: 危険や問題を知らせて、注意を促す。
cue: A colleague noticed a security gap and told the right people. Describe it.
reply: She raised the alarm before anyone else noticed.
transferCue: Describe how a neighbour helped during a flood.
transferReply: He raised the alarm at four in the morning.
nuance: About introduces the danger. It means warning others, not sounding a literal siren.

meaning: Stop trying because of past success.
easyEnglish: Stop trying because of past success.
japanese: 過去の成功に安住して、努力をやめる。
cue: A team had a strong year and has slowed down. Raise it carefully.
reply: We can't rest on our laurels after one good quarter.
transferCue: Describe a company that lost its lead.
transferReply: They rested on their laurels for five years and lost the market.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and laurels is always plural. Usually a warning rather than a description.

meaning: Vary the way something is done to keep it fresh.
easyEnglish: Vary the way something is done to keep it fresh.
japanese: やり方に変化をつけて、新鮮さを保つ。
cue: A friend is bored with the same weekly meals. Suggest variety.
reply: Ring the changes with one new recipe a week.
transferCue: Describe how a venue keeps its programme interesting.
transferReply: They ring the changes every season so regulars keep coming.
nuance: British. Changes is always plural, and on introduces what is being varied.

meaning: Be the one in control of a group.
easyEnglish: Be the one in control of a group.
japanese: その集団を、実質的に仕切っている。
cue: A friend jokes about who decides things in their house.
reply: The cat rules the roost in our flat.
transferCue: Describe an informal leader in a workplace.
transferReply: She isn't the manager, but she rules the roost.
nuance: Informal and often affectionate or teasing. It describes real influence rather than a formal title.

meaning: Ordinary, with nothing special about it.
easyEnglish: Ordinary, with nothing special about it.
japanese: ごく平凡で、特徴のない。
cue: A friend asks how a film was. It was watchable but forgettable.
reply: It was run of the mill, honestly. Fine but forgettable.
transferCue: Describe a hotel that met expectations exactly.
transferReply: The room was run of the mill but perfectly clean.
nuance: Written run-of-the-mill with hyphens before a noun. Mildly dismissive rather than negative.

meaning: Do something far better than someone else.
easyEnglish: Do something far better than someone else.
japanese: 相手を圧倒して、はるかに上を行く。
cue: A junior colleague outperformed everyone at a task. Describe it.
reply: She ran rings around the rest of us on the data work.
transferCue: Describe a one-sided sports match.
transferReply: They ran rings around us in the second half.
nuance: Rings is always plural; British English also says round. Admiring of the winner rather than mocking the loser.

meaning: Unhurt and out of danger.
easyEnglish: Unhurt and out of danger.
japanese: 無事で、けがもなく。
cue: A friend arrived after a difficult journey. Report it to their family.
reply: She got here safe and sound at midnight.
transferCue: Reassure someone about a package.
transferReply: The parcel arrived safe and sound this morning.
nuance: Fixed word order, usually after arrive, get or be. Warm and reassuring.

phrase: scrape the bottom of the barrel
meaning: Use the worst of what is left because nothing better remains.
easyEnglish: Use the worst of what is left because nothing better remains.
japanese: 残り物の中から、仕方なく選ぶ。
cue: Only weak candidates remain in a slow hiring round. Say it honestly.
reply: We're scraping the bottom of the barrel with this shortlist.
transferCue: Describe planning a meal at the end of the week.
transferReply: By Friday we're scraping the bottom of the barrel in the fridge.
frame: Scrape the bottom of the barrel
nuance: Critical of the quality available, not of the person choosing. Often shortened to scrape the barrel in British English.

meaning: An official or authoritative sign that something is acceptable.
easyEnglish: An official or authoritative sign that something is acceptable.
japanese: ここなら大丈夫という、お墨付き。
cue: A senior colleague endorsed your draft. Report it.
reply: It has her seal of approval, so we can circulate it.
transferCue: Describe a recommendation from your sister that convinced you.
transferReply: Her seal of approval matters more to me than any review.
frame: Give something your seal of approval
nuance: The possessive names who approves. Can be formal or playful depending on who gives it.

meaning: Describe your own abilities as less than they are.
easyEnglish: Describe your own abilities as less than they are.
japanese: 自分の力を、実際より低く見積もる。
cue: A colleague dismisses their own contribution. Correct them kindly.
reply: You're selling yourself short. You wrote the whole method.
transferCue: Advise a friend writing a job application.
transferReply: Don't sell yourself short in the first paragraph.
nuance: The reflexive follows the subject. Usually a gentle correction, so it pairs well with a specific example.

meaning: Fixed and impossible to change.
easyEnglish: Fixed and impossible to change.
japanese: 決定済みで、動かせない。
cue: A colleague worries that a draft schedule is final. Reassure them.
reply: Nothing is set in stone yet. Tell me what doesn't work.
transferCue: Explain which part of a plan cannot move.
transferReply: The launch date is set in stone; everything else can shift.
nuance: Very often negative: not set in stone, used to invite feedback. Stone takes no article.

meaning: Decide to aim for a particular goal.
easyEnglish: Decide to aim for a particular goal.
japanese: 目標を定めて、それを目指す。
cue: A friend has chosen one specific university. Describe their focus.
reply: She's set her sights on the marine biology course.
transferCue: Explain your own goal for the year.
transferReply: I've set my sights on finishing the draft by June.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and sights is always plural. It implies a single, chosen target.

meaning: Make something easier to understand.
easyEnglish: Make something easier to understand.
japanese: 分かりにくい点に、光を当てて説明する。
cue: A colleague's data explained a puzzling result. Acknowledge it.
reply: Your figures shed light on why March looked strange.
transferCue: Ask for help understanding a decision.
transferReply: Could you shed light on how the criteria were chosen?
nuance: On introduces the topic. Slightly formal, and often softened with some.

meaning: Brief and pleasant.
easyEnglish: Brief and pleasant.
japanese: 短くて、気持ちのよい。
cue: You are introducing a speaker with a tight schedule.
reply: I'll keep this short and sweet: here's Mira.
transferCue: Describe a message you sent after an interview.
transferReply: I kept the thank-you note short and sweet.
nuance: Usually with keep or be. It promises brevity, so the sentence after it should be brief.

meaning: Teach someone how a job is done.
easyEnglish: Teach someone how a job is done.
japanese: 仕事のやり方を、ひととおり教える。
cue: A new colleague starts on Monday. Offer to help them settle.
reply: I'll show you the ropes on your first morning.
transferCue: Thank someone who trained you.
transferReply: Thanks for showing me the ropes back in April.
nuance: The learner goes between show and the. Informal and friendly, about practical training.

meaning: Do nothing when action is needed.
easyEnglish: Do nothing when action is needed.
japanese: 動くべきときに、何もしないでいる。
cue: A problem is growing while approval is awaited. Urge action.
reply: We can't sit on our hands until the budget is signed.
transferCue: Describe a committee that delayed a decision.
transferReply: The board sat on its hands for six months.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Critical of inaction, so it works as an argument for acting.

meaning: Sleep very deeply and well.
easyEnglish: Sleep very deeply and well.
japanese: ぐっすり眠る。
cue: A friend asks how you slept after a long walk.
reply: I slept like a baby and woke up at nine.
transferCue: Describe how a change improved your rest.
transferReply: Since we moved the bed I sleep like a baby.
nuance: Means deeply, despite what babies actually do. Sleep like a log is the same idea.

meaning: Be forgotten.
easyEnglish: Be forgotten.
japanese: うっかり忘れる。
cue: You forgot to forward an email. Apologise without excuses.
reply: It completely slipped my mind. Sending it now.
transferCue: Explain a missed birthday to a friend.
transferReply: Your birthday slipped my mind in all the moving.
nuance: The forgotten thing is the subject. It sounds less careless than I forgot, but still apologises.

meaning: Start something that grows into a larger result later.
easyEnglish: Start something that grows into a larger result later.
japanese: のちに大きく育つものの、種をまく。
cue: An early decision caused later problems. Trace it.
reply: That contract sowed the seeds of the dispute.
transferCue: Describe how a teacher influenced your career.
transferReply: She sowed the seeds of my interest in geology.
nuance: Of introduces the later result, which can be good or bad. Seeds is always plural.

meaning: Show something clearly without words.
easyEnglish: Show something clearly without words.
japanese: 言葉以上に、多くを物語る。
cue: Nobody replied to a request for volunteers. Interpret the silence.
reply: The silence speaks volumes about how people feel.
transferCue: Describe what a small gesture showed.
transferReply: That she stayed until the end speaks volumes.
nuance: The evidence is the subject and about introduces what it reveals. Volumes is always plural.

meaning: Argue about differences too small to matter.
easyEnglish: Argue about differences too small to matter.
japanese: 取るに足りない細かい違いにこだわる。
cue: A discussion is stuck on two near-identical wordings. Move it on.
reply: We're splitting hairs. Either version says the same thing.
transferCue: Concede a point that does not really matter.
transferReply: I don't want to split hairs, so let's use yours.
nuance: Hairs is always plural. Usually about the discussion as a whole, which is less pointed than naming a person.

meaning: Take on so much that you cannot do any of it well.
easyEnglish: Take on so much that you cannot do any of it well.
japanese: 手を広げすぎて、どれも中途半端になる。
cue: A colleague has joined a fourth project. Raise your concern.
reply: I worry you're spreading yourself too thin.
transferCue: Explain why you turned down a committee.
transferReply: I said no because I was spreading myself too thin.
nuance: The reflexive follows the subject. Sympathetic rather than critical, so it works as gentle advice.

meaning: Refuse to change your position under pressure.
easyEnglish: Refuse to change your position under pressure.
japanese: 圧力に屈せず、自分の立場を守る。
cue: A colleague was pressed to lower an estimate but did not. Praise them.
reply: You stood your ground on the timeline, which was right.
transferCue: Advise a friend before a difficult negotiation.
transferReply: Stand your ground on the deposit. It's a reasonable request.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Approving, unlike dig your heels in, which suggests stubbornness.

meaning: Continue to the end despite difficulty.
easyEnglish: Continue to the end despite difficulty.
japanese: 困難があっても、最後までやり抜く。
cue: A long training programme is getting hard. Encourage a friend.
reply: Stay the course. Month four is the hardest one.
transferCue: Describe a team that finished a difficult project.
transferReply: Only two of us stayed the course to the end.
nuance: Course takes the, and the phrase implies a long, defined effort with an end point.

phrase: stick out like a sore thumb
meaning: Be very obviously different from everything around it.
easyEnglish: Be very obviously different from everything around it.
japanese: 周囲から浮いて、いやでも目立つ。
cue: One bright heading breaks an otherwise plain document. Point it out.
reply: That red heading sticks out like a sore thumb.
transferCue: Describe how you felt at a formal event.
transferReply: In trainers I stuck out like a sore thumb.
frame: Stick out like a sore thumb
nuance: Almost always negative about the thing that stands out. Stand out is an equally common version.
aliases: stand out like a sore thumb
stuck out like a sore thumb

meaning: Find a fair middle point between two things.
easyEnglish: Find a fair middle point between two things.
japanese: 二つのあいだで、ちょうどよい折り合いをつける。
cue: A policy is either too strict or too loose. Frame the problem.
reply: We need to strike a balance between speed and safety.
transferCue: Describe how you manage work and family time.
transferReply: I try to strike a balance by keeping evenings free.
frame: Strike a balance between A and B
nuance: Between introduces the two sides. Strike is the usual verb; find a balance is a plainer alternative.

meaning: Make people feel that something is true for them.
easyEnglish: Make people feel that something is true for them.
japanese: 人の心に響き、共感を呼ぶ。
cue: A talk clearly moved the audience. Describe the reaction.
reply: Her point about small teams struck a chord with everyone.
transferCue: Describe a book that stayed with you.
transferReply: The chapter about leaving home struck a chord.
nuance: With introduces the audience. It reports resonance, not agreement on every point.

meaning: Accept embarrassment in order to do the right thing.
easyEnglish: Accept embarrassment in order to do the right thing.
japanese: 恥をこらえて、意地を捨てる。
cue: A friend needs help but hates asking. Encourage them.
reply: Swallow your pride and ask. He'd want to know.
transferCue: Describe going back to a former employer.
transferReply: I swallowed my pride and asked for my old job back.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It respects the difficulty, so it encourages rather than scolds.

meaning: Formally disagree with something said or written.
easyEnglish: Formally disagree with something said or written.
japanese: 異議を唱える。
cue: A report's conclusion goes beyond its data. Object in a meeting.
reply: I take issue with the claim that this is settled.
transferCue: Disagree with one part of an otherwise good article.
transferReply: I'd take issue with the second section, but the rest is solid.
nuance: With introduces the claim. Formal and precise, which keeps disagreement about the argument.

meaning: Pause and think carefully about a situation.
easyEnglish: Pause and think carefully about a situation.
japanese: 立ち止まって、状況を見直す。
cue: A busy quarter has ended. Suggest a review.
reply: Let's take stock before we plan the next one.
transferCue: Describe what you did after a difficult year.
transferReply: I took stock and changed two things.
nuance: Of introduces what you review. No article before stock. It implies pausing, not acting.

meaning: Make something unpleasant slightly less intense.
easyEnglish: Make something unpleasant slightly less intense.
japanese: つらさや強さを、少しやわらげる。
cue: A friend is nervous before a talk. Suggest something small.
reply: A short walk might take the edge off the nerves.
transferCue: Describe a snack before a late dinner.
transferReply: I had an apple to take the edge off my hunger.
nuance: It reduces rather than removes, so it suits partial relief. Off introduces what is softened.

phrase: take the rough with the smooth
meaning: Accept the bad parts along with the good.
easyEnglish: Accept the bad parts along with the good.
japanese: よいことも悪いことも、まとめて受け入れる。
cue: A friend loves their freelance work but hates the uncertainty.
reply: You take the rough with the smooth. The freedom costs something.
transferCue: Describe living somewhere beautiful but remote.
transferReply: We take the rough with the smooth — the view is worth the drive.
frame: Take the rough with the smooth
nuance: British and fixed in form. It accepts a trade-off rather than complaining about it.

meaning: Talk about work when you are not at work.
easyEnglish: Talk about work when you are not at work.
japanese: 仕事を離れた場で、仕事の話をする。
cue: Two colleagues start discussing a project at a party. Interrupt lightly.
reply: No talking shop tonight. It's a birthday.
transferCue: Admit what you and a friend always end up doing.
transferReply: We meet for dinner and talk shop for two hours.
nuance: Shop takes no article. Mildly disapproving, usually said in social settings.

meaning: Do or say something that seems likely to bring bad luck.
easyEnglish: Do or say something that seems likely to bring bad luck.
japanese: わざわざ悪い結果を招くようなことを言う・する。
cue: A colleague says the week has been trouble-free. React playfully.
reply: Don't tempt fate. It's only Wednesday.
transferCue: Comment on a friend cancelling their insurance.
transferReply: Cancelling it the week before a trip is tempting fate.
nuance: Fate takes no article. Usually light and superstitious rather than a serious warning.

meaning: Try something in a small way to see how people react.
easyEnglish: Try something in a small way to see how people react.
japanese: 反応を見るために、小さく試してみる。
cue: You are unsure whether a new class would attract people. Suggest a trial.
reply: Let's test the water with one free session.
transferCue: Describe how you raised a sensitive idea at home.
transferReply: I tested the water by mentioning it once over dinner.
nuance: American English often uses waters. It describes a deliberate small trial before committing.

meaning: Someone or something that almost everyone knows.
easyEnglish: Someone or something that almost everyone knows.
japanese: 誰もが知っている、おなじみの存在。
cue: A small brand has become nationally known. Describe the change.
reply: Three years ago nobody had heard of them; now they're a household name.
transferCue: Describe a presenter your parents grew up with.
transferReply: She was a household name when my mother was young.
nuance: About recognition, not about respect. Usually within one country, so say where if it matters.

meaning: What you do only when nothing else has worked.
easyEnglish: What you do only when nothing else has worked.
japanese: ほかに手がないときの、最後の手段。
cue: A colleague suggests escalating immediately. Suggest keeping it in reserve.
reply: Let's keep that as a last resort and try email first.
transferCue: Explain why you took an expensive taxi.
transferReply: It was a last resort after both trains were cancelled.
nuance: Often with as. It signals reluctance, which makes an unpopular option easier to propose.

meaning: Far from happening or from being correct.
easyEnglish: Far from happening or from being correct.
japanese: 実現や正解には、まだ遠い。
cue: Someone asks whether a feature will ship this quarter.
reply: We're a long way off releasing it, honestly.
transferCue: Comment on an estimate that is well under the real cost.
transferReply: That figure is a long way off what the builder quoted.
frame: Be a long way off something
nuance: Followed by an -ing verb or a noun. It works for both time and accuracy.

meaning: Someone who does what they promise.
easyEnglish: Someone who does what they promise.
japanese: 約束を必ず守る人。
cue: A contractor did exactly what he said he would. Recommend him.
reply: He's a man of his word. The quote never changed.
transferCue: Describe a colleague who always delivers.
transferReply: She's a woman of her word, which is rarer than it should be.
frame: Be a man / woman of your word
nuance: The possessive matches the person. Both man and woman forms are used; as of your word for yourself.

meaning: Something where success depends mostly on trying many times.
easyEnglish: Something where success depends mostly on trying many times.
japanese: 数をこなすことが、結果を左右するもの。
cue: A friend is discouraged after six job applications. Offer perspective.
reply: Applying is a numbers game. Six isn't many yet.
transferCue: Describe how a sales team works.
transferReply: Cold calling is a numbers game, so they track attempts, not wins.
nuance: Numbers is always plural. It explains a process rather than excusing poor quality.

meaning: A difficult time, often from criticism or opposition.
easyEnglish: A difficult time, often from criticism or opposition.
japanese: 批判や反対にさらされる、苦しい時期。
cue: A proposal will face hard questions. Prepare a colleague.
reply: Expect a rough ride on Thursday. Bring the cost breakdown.
transferCue: Describe a politician's difficult interview.
transferReply: She had a rough ride on the morning programme.
frame: Have / give someone a rough ride
nuance: Used with have, get or give. It describes hostility received, not the difficulty of a task.

meaning: Someone reliable who will not make mistakes.
easyEnglish: Someone reliable who will not make mistakes.
japanese: 任せて安心できる、堅実な人。
cue: You are recommending someone to run a sensitive handover.
reply: Put Kenji on it. He's a safe pair of hands.
transferCue: Describe why a board chose a particular candidate.
transferReply: They wanted a safe pair of hands rather than a visionary.
frame: Be a safe pair of hands
nuance: Singular despite hands being plural. It praises reliability and can gently imply a lack of flair.

meaning: Something that gives new energy or encouragement.
easyEnglish: Something that gives new energy or encouragement.
japanese: 勢いを取り戻させる、ひと押し。
cue: A small grant revived a struggling project. Describe its effect.
reply: That funding was a shot in the arm for the whole team.
transferCue: Describe how good news affected a slow week.
transferReply: Her message was a shot in the arm on a bad Monday.
frame: Be a shot in the arm for something
nuance: For introduces who benefits. Always positive, and usually about morale or momentum.

meaning: Manage something in a very organised, disciplined way.
easyEnglish: Manage something in a very organised, disciplined way.
japanese: 規律よく、きっちりと組織を動かす。
cue: A department has no missed deadlines all year. Describe the manager.
reply: She runs a tight ship and it shows in the numbers.
transferCue: Describe a kitchen during a busy service.
transferReply: The head chef runs a tight ship on Friday nights.
nuance: Usually approving, though it can hint at strictness. Ship is always singular.

meaning: Affecting everyone or everything equally.
easyEnglish: Affecting everyone or everything equally.
japanese: 全体にわたって、一律に。
cue: A pay rise applies to every grade. Announce it clearly.
reply: The increase applies across the board, not just to new staff.
transferCue: Describe results that improved everywhere.
transferReply: Attendance rose across the board this term.
nuance: Comes after the verb; across-the-board with hyphens before a noun. It emphasises that nothing is excluded.

meaning: Although you believed it was the wrong choice.
easyEnglish: Although you believed it was the wrong choice.
japanese: よくないと分かっていながら。
cue: You agreed to something you doubted and it went badly. Reflect.
reply: I said yes against my better judgment and regretted it by Tuesday.
transferCue: Describe lending something you did not want to lend.
transferReply: Against my better judgment, I lent him the car.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. British spelling can be judgement; both are accepted.

meaning: Going to happen very soon.
easyEnglish: Going to happen very soon.
japanese: すぐそこまで来ている。
cue: A deadline is closer than the team realises. Remind them.
reply: The deadline is just around the corner, so let's prioritise.
transferCue: Comment on the changing season.
transferReply: Spring is around the corner — the light is back.
nuance: Often with just. It also has a literal sense of physical location, which context separates.

meaning: Usually, as a general pattern.
easyEnglish: Usually, as a general pattern.
japanese: 原則として、たいていは。
cue: A friend asks whether you work at weekends.
reply: As a rule I don't, but this month is unusual.
transferCue: Describe a policy that has exceptions.
transferReply: As a rule we don't refund after ninety days.
nuance: Opens a sentence or follows the subject. It leaves room for exceptions, unlike always.

meaning: Scarce and therefore valuable.
easyEnglish: Scarce and therefore valuable.
japanese: 数が少なく、価値が高い。
cue: Meeting rooms are hard to book this week. Explain.
reply: Space is at a premium while the annexe is closed.
transferCue: Describe time during a busy period.
transferReply: Time is at a premium in December, so we book early.
nuance: About scarcity rather than high price. Used with uncountable nouns like time, space and talent.

meaning: At maximum speed or effort.
easyEnglish: At maximum speed or effort.
japanese: 全速力で。全力で。
cue: Describe a production line before a holiday.
reply: The factory has been running at full tilt since October.
transferCue: Describe a child arriving home from school.
transferReply: He came through the door at full tilt.
nuance: Follows a verb of motion or activity. Slightly informal, and suggests it cannot be sustained.

meaning: Nearby and available, or about to happen.
easyEnglish: Nearby and available, or about to happen.
japanese: すぐ手の届くところにある。また、間近に迫っている。
cue: You are explaining how to prepare for a practical task.
reply: Keep a cloth at hand before you open the bottle.
transferCue: Describe a deadline in a formal note.
transferReply: With the review at hand, please send your notes by Friday.
frame: Keep something at hand / be at hand
nuance: Two senses: physically available and imminent. On hand is more common for supplies.

meaning: In your true nature, whatever you seem on the surface.
easyEnglish: In your true nature, whatever you seem on the surface.
japanese: 本質的には。心の底では。
cue: A colleague looks formal but loves practical work. Describe them.
reply: He wears a suit, but he's an engineer at heart.
transferCue: Describe why you keep returning to a small town.
transferReply: I'm a village person at heart.
nuance: Comes at the end of the description. It contrasts inner nature with outward appearance.

meaning: Immediately available to you.
easyEnglish: Immediately available to you.
japanese: すぐに使える状態で手元にある。
cue: You are describing a well-organised reference folder.
reply: Everything you need is at your fingertips in that folder.
transferCue: Describe what a good index gives a reader.
transferReply: A good index puts the whole book at your fingertips.
nuance: The possessive follows the person. About availability, not about skill.

meaning: Even if that is true, it does not change things.
easyEnglish: Even if that is true, it does not change things.
japanese: それはそうだとしても。
cue: Someone explains why a delay happened, but the deadline stands.
reply: Be that as it may, the client still needs it on Monday.
transferCue: Acknowledge a fair point before disagreeing.
transferReply: Be that as it may, I'd still rather not sign yet.
nuance: Formal and fixed, always at the start of a sentence. It concedes a point without accepting the conclusion.

meaning: So extreme that it is hard to accept.
easyEnglish: So extreme that it is hard to accept.
japanese: 信じられないほどである。
cue: A service failure was worse than anything you had seen. React.
reply: The wait was beyond belief — four hours with no update.
transferCue: Describe an unexpectedly generous act.
transferReply: Their kindness that week was beyond belief.
nuance: Comes after the noun or be. It works for very bad and very good extremes.

meaning: Stop yourself from saying what you think.
easyEnglish: Stop yourself from saying what you think.
japanese: 言いたいことをこらえる。
cue: You disagreed in a meeting but said nothing. Explain why.
reply: I bit my lip because the decision was already made.
transferCue: Advise a friend at a family gathering.
transferReply: You might have to bite your lip until the cake.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Similar to bite your tongue, which is slightly more common.

meaning: Publicly disagree with your own group.
easyEnglish: Publicly disagree with your own group.
japanese: 味方であるはずの集団に、公然と異を唱える。
cue: One committee member disagreed publicly. Describe it.
reply: She broke ranks and said the timetable was unworkable.
transferCue: Describe a minister's unexpected statement.
transferReply: Two of them broke ranks over the funding cut.
nuance: Ranks is always plural. With introduces the group. It implies a visible, deliberate break.

meaning: According to what everyone says.
easyEnglish: According to what everyone says.
japanese: 誰の話を聞いても。伝え聞くところでは。
cue: You did not attend an event but heard about it. Report it.
reply: By all accounts it was a good evening.
transferCue: Describe a new colleague you have not met.
transferReply: By all accounts she's very good with clients.
nuance: Usually opens a sentence. It marks second-hand information, which keeps you from overstating.

meaning: Certainly; please do.
easyEnglish: Certainly; please do.
japanese: ぜひどうぞ。もちろん構いません。
cue: Someone asks whether they may take a photograph.
reply: By all means. The light is better from that side.
transferCue: Agree to a colleague's request to join a call.
transferReply: By all means join us. I'll forward the invitation.
nuance: A polite, slightly formal yes. Means is always plural even in this fixed phrase.

meaning: By a very large amount.
easyEnglish: By a very large amount.
japanese: はるかに。断然。
cue: One option is clearly better than the rest. Say so.
reply: This is by far the simplest of the three.
transferCue: Describe the busiest month of your year.
transferReply: March is by far our busiest month.
frame: By far the most / the best
nuance: Used with superlatives and comparatives. It usually comes before the.

meaning: Not at all.
easyEnglish: Not at all.
japanese: 決して〜ではない。
cue: Someone assumes a decision is final. Correct that impression.
reply: That's by no means settled. Two people still disagree.
transferCue: Qualify praise of your own work.
transferReply: It's by no means finished, but the structure is there.
nuance: A formal negative. At the start of a sentence it inverts the verb: by no means is it settled.

meaning: Make people doubt something.
easyEnglish: Make people doubt something.
japanese: 疑いを投げかける。信頼性を揺るがす。
cue: A new finding undermines an earlier report. Describe the effect.
reply: These results call into question the whole method.
transferCue: Describe how one error affected trust in a document.
transferReply: One wrong date can call into question everything else in it.
nuance: Formal. The object can sit between call and into, or after into question.

meaning: Try to remember something from the past.
easyEnglish: Try to remember something from the past.
japanese: 過去のことを思い起こす。
cue: You want a colleague to recall an old meeting.
reply: Cast your mind back to the March review — who raised it?
transferCue: Introduce a memory in a speech.
transferReply: I cast my mind back to our first office above the bakery.
frame: Cast your mind back to something
nuance: To introduces the time or event. Slightly formal, and it invites rather than tests memory.

meaning: Become known after being hidden.
easyEnglish: Become known after being hidden.
japanese: 隠れていたことが、明らかになる。
cue: An old problem surfaced during an audit. Report it neutrally.
reply: The discrepancy came to light during the audit.
transferCue: Describe how a family story emerged.
transferReply: The letters came to light when we cleared the attic.
nuance: The fact is the subject, not the person who found it. Neutral, so it avoids assigning blame.

meaning: End without any result.
easyEnglish: End without any result.
japanese: 結局、何にもならずに終わる。
cue: A long negotiation produced no agreement. Summarise.
reply: Six months of talks came to nothing.
transferCue: Describe a hopeful lead that faded.
transferReply: The introduction came to nothing, but I learned a lot.
nuance: The effort is the subject. It reports a result without blaming anyone.

meaning: Whatever happens.
easyEnglish: Whatever happens.
japanese: 何が起ころうとも。
cue: A friend worries you might cancel again. Reassure them.
reply: I'll be there on Saturday, come what may.
transferCue: Commit to finishing something difficult.
transferReply: Come what may, we're submitting on the thirtieth.
nuance: Fixed and slightly literary. It sits at the start or end of a sentence, set off by a comma.

meaning: Something that everyone in a group already knows.
easyEnglish: Something that everyone in a group already knows.
japanese: みんなが知っている、周知の事実。
cue: Someone worries about sharing a fact that is already public.
reply: It's common knowledge by now. It was in the newsletter.
transferCue: Correct an assumption that a fact was secret.
transferReply: I thought it was common knowledge that she'd moved teams.
nuance: Uncountable, so no article. It refers to a specific group, so say who if it matters.

meaning: Hope that something goes well.
easyEnglish: Hope that something goes well.
japanese: うまくいくように願う。
cue: A friend is waiting on a decision tomorrow. Wish them luck.
reply: I'll cross my fingers for you tomorrow.
transferCue: Describe waiting for a delayed train connection.
transferReply: We crossed our fingers and made the last connection.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and fingers is plural. Keep your fingers crossed is equally common.

meaning: Get your first experience of a kind of work.
easyEnglish: Get your first experience of a kind of work.
japanese: その分野での経験を、最初に積む。
cue: A colleague asks where you learned to handle difficult clients.
reply: I cut my teeth on complaints at a call centre.
transferCue: Describe where a well-known figure started.
transferReply: She cut her teeth on local radio before television.
nuance: On introduces the early work, and the possessive follows the subject. It implies formative experience.

meaning: Extremely tired.
easyEnglish: Extremely tired.
japanese: 立っていられないほど疲れている。
cue: A colleague has worked two long shifts. Send them home.
reply: You're dead on your feet. Go home and finish tomorrow.
transferCue: Describe how you felt after a long day of travel.
transferReply: By the time we checked in I was dead on my feet.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Informal and hyperbolic; it is about tiredness only.

meaning: Perform a small ceremonial task for a group.
easyEnglish: Perform a small ceremonial task for a group.
japanese: その場の役目を、代表して務める。
cue: A cake needs cutting at a small party. Invite someone.
reply: Would you do the honours and cut the first slice?
transferCue: Ask someone to pour the drinks.
transferReply: You brought it, so you should do the honours.
nuance: Honours is always plural; American English spells it honors. Light and slightly ceremonious.

meaning: At some point in the future.
easyEnglish: At some point in the future.
japanese: この先、いずれ。
cue: A decision can wait but will matter later. Note it.
reply: We'll need a bigger server down the line, not this year.
transferCue: Describe a consequence of a choice made now.
transferReply: Choosing the cheaper option costs more down the line.
nuance: American English often says down the road. Often with further or somewhere for vagueness.

meaning: Be the one given the least pleasant task.
easyEnglish: Be the one given the least pleasant task.
japanese: いちばん嫌な役回りを引き当てる。
cue: Someone has to work on a public holiday. Describe who.
reply: I drew the short straw and I'm covering the holiday.
transferCue: Describe how a family decided who drives.
transferReply: My brother drew the short straw and drove both ways.
nuance: Straw is singular and takes the. It implies chance rather than an unfair decision.

meaning: Stop being careful and become vulnerable.
easyEnglish: Stop being careful and become vulnerable.
japanese: 警戒をゆるめて、隙を見せる。
cue: A careful process failed in the final week. Explain how.
reply: We dropped our guard in the last week and missed the check.
transferCue: Describe becoming comfortable with new people.
transferReply: It took a month before I dropped my guard with them.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Negative about carelessness, positive about trusting people.

meaning: That is reasonable; I accept it.
easyEnglish: That is reasonable; I accept it.
japanese: なるほど、もっともだ。
cue: A friend explains why they cannot come. Accept it warmly.
reply: Fair enough. Let's find another weekend.
transferCue: Accept a colleague's objection to a deadline.
transferReply: Fair enough — let's move it to Wednesday.
nuance: Informal, usually a full response on its own. It accepts a reason without necessarily agreeing.

meaning: Something people may reasonably criticise or pursue.
easyEnglish: Something people may reasonably criticise or pursue.
japanese: 批判や追及の対象にされても仕方がないもの。
cue: A public figure's policy is criticised, but their family is not. Draw the line.
reply: Her policies are fair game; her children are not.
transferCue: Describe what a review may cover.
transferReply: Anything we published is fair game for the review.
nuance: Uncountable, so no article. It marks something as legitimately open to criticism.

meaning: Look for and point out problems in something.
easyEnglish: Look for and point out problems in something.
japanese: あら探しをして、欠点を指摘する。
cue: A colleague criticises every version of a document. Describe it.
reply: He finds fault with every draft but never suggests wording.
transferCue: Describe how you try to give feedback.
transferReply: I try not to find fault with the parts that are working.
nuance: With introduces the target. Fault stays singular, and the phrase is usually critical of the critic.

meaning: Most importantly, before anything else.
easyEnglish: Most importantly, before anything else.
japanese: 何よりもまず。
cue: You are explaining your priority in a short speech.
reply: First and foremost, thank you for staying late this week.
transferCue: Describe how you see your own role.
transferReply: First and foremost I'm a teacher, and the admin comes second.
nuance: Opens a sentence, followed by a comma. Slightly formal, and stronger than simply first.

meaning: In every practical sense, if not officially.
easyEnglish: In every practical sense, if not officially.
japanese: 実質的には。事実上。
cue: A colleague acts as team lead without the title. Describe the situation.
reply: For all intents and purposes she already runs the team.
transferCue: Describe a project that is finished apart from paperwork.
transferReply: For all intents and purposes it's done. Only signatures remain.
nuance: Formal and fixed; it is not for all intensive purposes. It contrasts practice with formal status.

meaning: Whether the result is good or bad.
easyEnglish: Whether the result is good or bad.
japanese: よかれあしかれ。
cue: A decision has already been made and cannot change. Accept it.
reply: For better or worse, we've chosen the new system.
transferCue: Describe a change in your neighbourhood.
transferReply: For better or worse, the whole street has changed.
nuance: Usually opens a sentence. It accepts uncertainty about the outcome rather than predicting it.

meaning: Mostly, though not entirely.
easyEnglish: Mostly, though not entirely.
japanese: おおむね。大部分は。
cue: A process works well with occasional problems. Summarise it.
reply: For the most part it runs itself, apart from Mondays.
transferCue: Describe your experience of a long course.
transferReply: For the most part the teaching was excellent.
nuance: Opens a sentence or follows the verb. It leaves room for exceptions, so it reads as honest.

meaning: Do something harmful to someone because they harmed you.
easyEnglish: Do something harmful to someone because they harmed you.
japanese: 仕返しをして、貸し借りをなしにする。
cue: A friend wants revenge for an unfair review. Advise against it.
reply: Trying to get even will cost you more than it costs them.
transferCue: Describe a rivalry that ended well.
transferReply: They stopped trying to get even and started sharing customers.
nuance: With introduces the person. Informal, and usually the thing being advised against.

meaning: Make no progress at all.
easyEnglish: Make no progress at all.
japanese: まったく進展しない。
cue: Three calls to support produced nothing. Report it.
reply: I've called twice and got nowhere.
transferCue: Describe an argument that went in circles.
transferReply: We argued for an hour and got nowhere.
nuance: With introduces the task or person. Get nowhere fast adds emphasis, not speed.

phrase: get on like a house on fire
meaning: Like each other immediately and very much.
easyEnglish: Like each other immediately and very much.
japanese: すぐに意気投合して、とても仲よくなる。
cue: Two friends you introduced became close at once. Describe it.
reply: They got on like a house on fire from the first evening.
transferCue: Describe meeting a colleague's family.
transferReply: My mother and his sister get on like a house on fire.
frame: Get on like a house on fire
nuance: British; American English says get along. Warm and positive despite the alarming image.

meaning: Approximately, allowing a small difference.
easyEnglish: Approximately, allowing a small difference.
japanese: 多少の誤差はあるとして、おおよそ。
cue: A friend asks how long the journey takes.
reply: About two hours, give or take twenty minutes.
transferCue: Estimate how many people attended an event.
transferReply: There were sixty people, give or take.
nuance: Follows a figure, usually after a comma, with or without the margin stated.

meaning: Accidentally reveal a secret.
easyEnglish: Accidentally reveal a secret.
japanese: うっかり秘密を明かしてしまう。
cue: Someone nearly revealed a surprise party. Warn them.
reply: Don't mention the cake or you'll give the game away.
transferCue: Describe how a secret was discovered.
transferReply: His face gave the game away before he spoke.
nuance: The person or the sign can be the subject. About accidental revelation, not deliberate telling.

meaning: Treat someone gently, or use less of something.
easyEnglish: Treat someone gently, or use less of something.
japanese: 手加減する。控えめにする。
cue: A new colleague made a first-week mistake. Ask for leniency.
reply: Go easy on him. It's his first week.
transferCue: Ask someone to use less of an ingredient.
transferReply: Go easy on the chilli — my father doesn't like heat.
nuance: On introduces the person or the ingredient. Informal, and usually a request rather than a rule.

meaning: Share the cost of something equally.
easyEnglish: Share the cost of something equally.
japanese: 費用を半分ずつ出し合う。
cue: You and a friend are buying a gift together. Propose the split.
reply: Shall we go halves on the present?
transferCue: Describe how two housemates bought a shared item.
transferReply: We went halves on the washing machine.
nuance: On introduces what is shared. Halves is always plural, and it means exactly two shares.

meaning: Explain something thoroughly.
easyEnglish: Explain something thoroughly.
japanese: 細かいところまで詳しく説明する。
cue: A colleague asks a question you cannot answer fully in a meeting.
reply: I won't go into detail now, but I'll write it up this afternoon.
transferCue: Decline to discuss a private matter.
transferReply: I'd rather not go into detail, but it's being handled.
nuance: Detail is usually singular here. Very often negative, as a polite way to keep something brief.

meaning: Do something by yourself instead of with others.
easyEnglish: Do something by yourself instead of with others.
japanese: 人と組まず、単独でやる。
cue: A colleague is considering leaving to start a business. Reflect it back.
reply: So you're thinking of going it alone after five years here?
transferCue: Describe a musician leaving a band.
transferReply: She went it alone and released the album herself.
nuance: Fixed with it, which has no reference. Neutral to admiring about independence.

meaning: Keep discussing something without making progress.
easyEnglish: Keep discussing something without making progress.
japanese: 堂々巡りで、話が先に進まない。
cue: A meeting keeps returning to the same point. Interrupt usefully.
reply: We're going round in circles. Shall we vote?
transferCue: Describe a decision you could not make alone.
transferReply: I went round in circles for a week before asking for advice.
nuance: British uses round, American around. Circles is always plural.

meaning: Be destroyed or come to nothing.
easyEnglish: Be destroyed or come to nothing.
japanese: すべて台なしになる。
cue: A cancellation destroyed months of planning. Describe it.
reply: Six months of planning went up in smoke in one email.
transferCue: Describe a savings plan hit by an emergency.
transferReply: The deposit went up in smoke when the boiler failed.
nuance: The plan or money is the subject. Dramatic, and it implies a sudden total loss.

meaning: Working very closely together.
easyEnglish: Working very closely together.
japanese: ぴったりと連携して。
cue: Two departments coordinated unusually well. Describe it.
reply: Design and support worked hand in glove on this release.
transferCue: Describe two organisations with a close arrangement.
transferReply: The two charities operate hand in glove.
frame: Work hand in glove with someone
nuance: No articles inside the phrase. It can hint at collusion, so tone matters.

meaning: Fixed and not open to exceptions.
easyEnglish: Fixed and not open to exceptions.
japanese: 例外を認めない、厳格な。
cue: A colleague asks whether a guideline can flex.
reply: There's no hard and fast rule. Use your judgement.
transferCue: Describe one requirement that cannot change.
transferReply: The safety check is a hard and fast rule.
nuance: Almost always before rule or rules, and very often negative: no hard and fast rule.

meaning: Enjoy an opportunity to do something, often at others' expense.
easyEnglish: Enjoy an opportunity to do something, often at others' expense.
japanese: ここぞとばかりに、思う存分やる。
cue: A public mistake will attract heavy commentary. Predict the reaction.
reply: The press will have a field day with this.
transferCue: Describe children in a new playground.
transferReply: The kids had a field day on the climbing frame.
frame: Have a field day with something
nuance: With introduces the material. Often about critics enjoying someone's difficulty, but it can be innocent.

meaning: Have a personal interest in how something turns out.
easyEnglish: Have a personal interest in how something turns out.
japanese: 結果に自分の利害が関わっている。
cue: Explain why a department should be consulted.
reply: They have a stake in this, so they should see the draft.
transferCue: Describe why residents joined a planning meeting.
transferReply: Everyone on the street has a stake in the decision.
nuance: In introduces the matter. It can mean financial ownership or simply a personal interest.

meaning: Want to cause trouble for someone because you dislike them.
easyEnglish: Want to cause trouble for someone because you dislike them.
japanese: 目の敵にして、つらく当たる。
cue: A friend feels singled out by one colleague. Reflect their view.
reply: You feel like she has it in for you, is that right?
transferCue: Reassure someone who suspects unfair treatment.
transferReply: I don't think anyone has it in for you. The rota is random.
nuance: For introduces the target. A serious accusation, so it is often softened with I think or it feels like.

meaning: Reduce risk by not committing to one option.
easyEnglish: Reduce risk by not committing to one option.
japanese: ひとつに賭けず、危険を分散する。
cue: A colleague has applied to two very different programmes. Describe it.
reply: She's hedging her bets with two applications.
transferCue: Explain why you booked a refundable ticket.
transferReply: I hedged my bets and paid extra for the flexible fare.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and bets is plural. Neutral to slightly critical of indecision.

meaning: Have great and often sudden success or luck.
easyEnglish: Have great and often sudden success or luck.
japanese: 大当たりを引く。
cue: A friend found a perfect flat on the first viewing. React.
reply: You hit the jackpot with that one.
transferCue: Describe an unexpectedly good hire.
transferReply: We hit the jackpot when she applied.
nuance: Informal and always positive. It implies luck as much as effort.

meaning: Remain believable when examined.
easyEnglish: Remain believable when examined.
japanese: 検討に耐えて、筋が通る。
cue: An explanation collapses under questioning. Say so.
reply: That explanation doesn't hold water when you check the dates.
transferCue: Confirm that an argument survived scrutiny.
transferReply: Her theory holds water even with the new data.
nuance: The argument is the subject. Water takes no article, and the phrase is most common in the negative.

meaning: Perform as well as the others around you.
easyEnglish: Perform as well as the others around you.
japanese: 周囲に引けを取らずにやれる。
cue: A junior colleague kept up with much more experienced people. Praise them.
reply: You held your own in a room of specialists.
transferCue: Describe a small team competing with large ones.
transferReply: They hold their own against companies ten times the size.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and against introduces the comparison. Quiet praise for keeping up.

meaning: In a difficult situation that is hard to escape.
easyEnglish: In a difficult situation that is hard to escape.
japanese: 身動きの取れない、困った状況にある。
cue: Your only key broke in the lock before work. Ask for help.
reply: I'm in a fix — could I borrow your spare key?
transferCue: Describe a team that lost a supplier suddenly.
transferReply: The cancellation left us in a fix for two weeks.
nuance: British and informal; American English says in a bind. It describes circumstances, not a mistake.

meaning: In practice, whatever the formal position is.
easyEnglish: In practice, whatever the formal position is.
japanese: 実際のところは。事実上。
cue: A rule is technically optional but everyone follows it. Explain.
reply: In effect it's compulsory, even though the wording says optional.
transferCue: Describe a discount that cancels a price rise.
transferReply: In effect, the price hasn't changed at all.
nuance: Slightly formal. Distinct from in force, which means officially applying.

meaning: Very clearly and forcefully.
easyEnglish: Very clearly and forcefully.
japanese: はっきりと、強い調子で。
cue: Someone made their objection unmistakably clear. Report it.
reply: She told them in no uncertain terms that it wasn't acceptable.
transferCue: Describe a firm boundary you set.
transferReply: I said in no uncertain terms that I wouldn't work Sundays.
frame: Tell someone in no uncertain terms
nuance: A double negative meaning very clearly. Terms is always plural, and it usually follows a verb of speaking.

meaning: Involved in something too difficult for you.
easyEnglish: Involved in something too difficult for you.
japanese: 手に余ることに関わってしまっている。
cue: A colleague has taken on a task beyond their experience. Offer help.
reply: Say so if you're in over your head. I can take half.
transferCue: Admit you underestimated a project.
transferReply: I was in over my head by the second week.
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Sympathetic rather than critical, so it makes asking for help easier.

meaning: Mentioned briefly, not as the main point.
easyEnglish: Mentioned briefly, not as the main point.
japanese: 本題のついでに、ちらりと。
cue: You heard something as a side remark. Report it carefully.
reply: He mentioned it in passing, so I don't know the detail.
transferCue: Raise a small point at the end of a meeting.
transferReply: Just in passing — the printer is out of paper again.
nuance: Usually after mention or say. It lowers the weight of what follows.

meaning: Despite having to deal with something difficult.
easyEnglish: Despite having to deal with something difficult.
japanese: 困難に直面しながらも。
cue: A team delivered despite serious obstacles. Recognise it.
reply: They finished in the face of real difficulty.
transferCue: Describe someone who stayed calm under criticism.
transferReply: She stayed polite in the face of a lot of anger.
nuance: Followed by a noun. Slightly formal, and usually introduces adversity rather than opportunity.

meaning: At the very beginning, before anything else happened.
easyEnglish: At the very beginning, before anything else happened.
japanese: そもそも。最初の段階で。
cue: A problem could have been avoided from the start. Point it out.
reply: We shouldn't have accepted the date in the first place.
transferCue: Explain why you joined a group.
transferReply: I joined in the first place because of the evening classes.
nuance: Comes at the end of the clause. It often carries mild regret about an original decision.

meaning: In person, rather than in a picture or on a screen.
easyEnglish: In person, rather than in a picture or on a screen.
japanese: 写真や画面越しではなく、実物で。
cue: You finally met a long-time remote colleague. Describe it.
reply: It was strange to meet her in the flesh after four years of calls.
transferCue: Describe seeing a famous painting.
transferReply: It's much smaller in the flesh than in photographs.
nuance: Used for people and sometimes objects. It marks a contrast with images or screens.

meaning: In a position where you face hard questions or pressure.
easyEnglish: In a position where you face hard questions or pressure.
japanese: 厳しい追及や重圧を受ける立場にある。
cue: A colleague will answer for a decision at a board meeting. Describe it.
reply: She's in the hot seat on Thursday about the overspend.
transferCue: Describe a manager after a public failure.
transferReply: The director has been in the hot seat all week.
nuance: About pressure and accountability, not about being in charge generally.

meaning: Following something, usually as a result of it.
easyEnglish: Following something, usually as a result of it.
japanese: 〜を受けて、その後に。
cue: New rules followed a well-known incident. Describe the sequence.
reply: The rules were introduced in the wake of the accident.
transferCue: Describe changes after a company reorganisation.
transferReply: In the wake of the merger, three teams were combined.
nuance: Formal, followed by a noun. It usually follows a difficult event rather than a happy one.

meaning: According to the plan or idea, though maybe not in practice.
easyEnglish: According to the plan or idea, though maybe not in practice.
japanese: 理屈のうえでは。建前としては。
cue: A process should work but never quite does. Explain.
reply: In theory it takes ten minutes. In practice, half a day.
transferCue: Describe an entitlement people rarely use.
transferReply: In theory everyone gets study leave.
nuance: Usually paired with in practice for contrast. It signals scepticism without contradicting anyone.

meaning: One after another, or as a result of that.
easyEnglish: One after another, or as a result of that.
japanese: 順番に。また、その結果として。
cue: You are explaining how a meeting will run.
reply: We'll hear from each team in turn, five minutes each.
transferCue: Describe a chain of effects.
transferReply: The delay raised costs, which in turn reduced the margin.
nuance: Two senses: one by one, and consequently. The second usually sits inside a clause after which.

meaning: Damage the relationship between two people.
easyEnglish: Damage the relationship between two people.
japanese: 二人のあいだに入って、関係を損なう。
cue: A disagreement about money is affecting two friends. Warn gently.
reply: Don't let one invoice come between you.
transferCue: Describe a family that stayed close despite a dispute.
transferReply: Nothing has ever come between those two sisters.
nuance: Inseparable, and it needs two people or a plural. The cause is the subject.

meaning: Someone who ignores the rules everyone else follows.
easyEnglish: Someone who ignores the rules everyone else follows.
japanese: 周りの決まりを気にせず、自分のやり方を通す人。
cue: A colleague files reports in their own format every month. Describe them.
reply: He's a law unto himself when it comes to paperwork.
transferCue: Describe a cat that ignores every routine.
transferReply: That cat is a law unto herself.
nuance: The reflexive follows the subject. Usually half-exasperated and half-admiring.

phrase: take a turn for the worse
meaning: Suddenly become worse.
easyEnglish: Suddenly become worse.
japanese: 急に悪いほうへ向かう。
cue: A situation that was improving has deteriorated. Report it.
reply: Things took a turn for the worse after the second delay.
transferCue: Describe weather on a hiking day.
transferReply: The weather took a turn for the worse around noon.
frame: Take a turn for the worse / better
nuance: Better and worse both work. The situation, not a person, is the subject.
aliases: take a turn for the better
took a turn for the worse

meaning: Whatever else is true; in any case.
easyEnglish: Whatever else is true; in any case.
japanese: いずれにしても。とにかく。
cue: Details are unclear but one thing is certain. Move the discussion on.
reply: At any rate, we can't start before the permit arrives.
transferCue: Correct yourself mid-sentence.
transferReply: It was Tuesday — at any rate, it was early in the week.
nuance: Usually opens a clause with a comma. It sets aside uncertain detail and keeps the main point.

meaning: Misunderstanding each other because you are talking about different things.
